operations.description: Creates an inbox that sends and receives email at an address on one of your domains. The domain must belong to the team. Without `forwarding`, the domain must have receiving enabled, with DKIM and SPF verified and the inbound MX record verified or pending. With `forwarding` set to `true`, the domain only needs DKIM and SPF verified for sending, and Resend generates a `receiving_address` on the team inbound domain, and a team without an inbound domain gets a 422. A domain that does not meet these rules returns a 422 validation_error. An address or receiving address that is already in use returns a 409. A team that has reached the inbox limit of its plan returns a 403 validation_error. A blocked account returns a 451.

operations.summary: Creates an unsent draft in an inbox, either as a new thread or as a reply in an existing thread. Supply at least one non-empty recipient, subject, body, or attachment field; reply drafts require both `thread_id` and `reply_to_email_id`. If a reply draft already exists for the target email, the response returns its ID and only a supplied `attachments` value is applied.
operations.description: Creates an unsent draft on the inbox. Omit `thread_id` and `reply_to_email_id` for a draft that starts a new thread. Pass both together for a reply draft in an existing thread. A reply draft without `to` is addressed to the sender of the email it replies to, or to its Reply-To when set. For an email the inbox sent, it defaults to that email's `to` recipients. Send `to: []` to leave it empty. At least one of `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `text`, `html` or `attachments` must be non-empty. The combined recipients of `to`, `cc` and `bcc` cannot exceed 50. Attachments are stored on the draft, so each one needs `content`, `filename` and `content_type`. Returns 201 for a new draft. Only one unsent reply draft can target an email, so a reply draft request for an email that already has one returns 200 with the ID of the existing draft. An unknown `thread_id`, or a `reply_to_email_id` that is not in that thread, returns a 404. That request ignores every other field, except `attachments`, which replaces the attachments of the existing draft when sent. A reply draft created without `subject` stores an empty subject and gets no `Re:` prefix, so set one before you send it.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key for the request, so the draft is created only once. A retry with the same key within 24 hours returns the first successful (2xx) response, with the `idempotent-replayed: true` header. A failed request is not stored, so it can be retried with the same key. Reusing the key with a different body, or while the first request is still running, returns a 409. An empty key, or one longer than 256 characters, returns a 400 `invalid_idempotency_key`. [Learn more](https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/emails/idempotency-keys)

parameters.name: inbox_id
parameters.description: The Inbox ID. An email address is not accepted.

parameters.name: inbox_id

Supply `to` recipients and optionally add a note with `html` or `text`; the original message is quoted and its attachments are included. Added attachments share the original message's limit of 10 files and 25 MB of content.
operations.description: Forwards a message from the inbox address right away, with no stored draft. The original message is quoted under a forwarded-message banner, below the optional `html` or `text` note. The attachments of the original message are sent with the forward, together with any `attachments` you add. The request fails when they exceed 10 files or 25 MB of `content` in total. An original attachment that was sent from a URL (`path`) cannot be forwarded, and the request returns a 422. The whole email, encoded, can be at most 40 MB, or the request returns a 422.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key for the request, so the forward is sent only once. A retry with the same key within 24 hours returns the first successful (2xx) response, with the `idempotent-replayed: true` header. A failed request is not stored, so it can be retried with the same key. Reusing the key with a different body, or while the first request is still running, returns a 409. An empty key, or one longer than 256 characters, returns a 400 `invalid_idempotency_key`. [Learn more](https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/emails/idempotency-keys)

parameters.name: inbox_id

Use `html` or `text` for the reply body; recipients are derived from the message, with `reply_all` controlling whether other recipients are copied. The reply is threaded under the original message.
operations.description: Sends a reply from the inbox address right away, with no stored draft. The `to` recipients come from the message you reply to. For a message the inbox received, the reply goes to its `Reply-To` addresses, or to its sender when it has no `Reply-To`. For a message the inbox sent, the reply goes to that message's `to` recipients. Set `reply_all` to also copy the other recipients of the message. The reply threads under the message through the `In-Reply-To` and `References` headers. When no recipient can be found for the reply, the request returns a 422. The whole email, encoded, can be at most 40 MB, or the request returns a 422.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key for the request, so the reply is sent only once. A retry with the same key within 24 hours returns the first successful (2xx) response, with the `idempotent-replayed: true` header. A failed request is not stored, so it can be retried with the same key. Reusing the key with a different body, or while the first request is still running, returns a 409. operations.summary: Searches an inbox’s threads by email text, sender or recipient, attachment presence, and date. Results are ordered by latest activity, newest first, and paginate like the list threads endpoint, so a cursor that is not a thread ID returns a 422. Search can be up to about a minute behind new emails. Different parameters combine, so a thread must match all of them. `folders`, `labels`, and `read` apply to the thread. `query`, `from`, `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `has_attachment`, `start_date`, and `end_date` must all match the same email in the thread. When any of these email filters is set, the matching email must itself be in one of `folders`. For `sent`, that means an email the inbox sent. parameters.name: end_date

properties.description: Recipient email address. For multiple addresses, send as an array of strings. Must name at least one address. `to`, `cc` and `bcc` combined cannot exceed 50 recipients. properties.name: cc
properties.description: CC recipient email address. For multiple addresses, send as an array of strings. Counts toward the 50-recipient limit. Each address is `email@example.com` or `Name <email@example.com>`. An address that is not valid returns a 422.

properties.name: bcc
properties.description: BCC recipient email address. For multiple addresses, send as an array of strings. Counts toward the 50-recipient limit. Each address is `email@example.com` or `Name <email@example.com>`. An address that is not valid returns a 422.

properties.name: subject
properties.description: The subject of the forward. Cannot be only whitespace or contain a line break. When omitted, the thread subject is used, prefixed with `Fwd:` if it does not already start with it.

properties.name: attachments
properties.description: Files to attach, as on `POST /emails`. Each one needs `content` or `path`. They share one limit with the attachments of the original message, which the forward also sends. Together they can have up to 10 files and at most 25 MB of `content`. A `path` file counts toward the 10 files only, because it is fetched when the email is sent. An empty file, a blocked file type, a `path` that is not an `http` or `https` URL or that points to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `0.0.0.0`, or a `content_type` that is not a valid MIME type returns a 422.

properties.description: Custom headers to add to the email. The `In-Reply-To`, `References` and `Reply-To` headers are set by Resend and cannot be set here. Header names cannot be empty, and names and values cannot contain line breaks or null characters, or the request returns a 422. `null` means no custom headers.
